subject: Post-call: OpsWave deployment commitments & capacity scan
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Park <lpark@opswave.com>, Ben Cho <bcho@opswave.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-05T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap + technical notes (OpsWave)

Thanks again for the call earlier today — good conversation. Below is a short recap of the technical commitments and the capacity snapshot we discussed, plus clear next steps so everyone has the same view.

High-level pain points (your description):
- User-facing inference tails currently spiking to 600–800ms p95 during peak promos; inconsistent tail behavior leads to failed client-side timeouts.
- Cost pressure with current vendor (~$200 per 1M tokens at observed throughput).
- Need a deployment that keeps data in the US and integrates with SSO/KMS.
- Expect seasonal bursts (promo spikes) up to ~3x baseline QPS for short windows.

Goals we aligned on:
- Target p95 latency <= 220ms for single-turn generative calls at nominal load.
- Stable concurrent throughput of ~80 req/s for the main endpoint with graceful 3x burst handling.
- Latency SLOs tied to per-route routing policy and automatic fallback to lower-cost model variant when needed.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 artifacts + traceable audit logs.

Technical notes / suggested topology (From Redwood):
- Recommended: Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) in us-west with autoscaled burst capacity and a warm-host fallback path to our hosted fleet.
- Kernel/config: use int8 quantized TGI-compatible weights for 4k-context models; prefix KV caching for common prompt templates to reduce tokens rendered.
- Batching: adaptive batching target ~8–16 requests per batch for your median seq lengths (~1k tokens).
- Caching: local per-instance KV cache + global prefix cache for queries that hit the decisioning templates.
- Routing: policy-based routing by SLO (latency-first for checkout, cost-first for async tasks).

What we need from OpsWave (next items):
1) Sample traffic profile + small dataset of representative requests (I attached opswave_metrics_sample.csv).
2) Security/compliance checklist you want completed (I attached OpsWave_SOC2_Request.pdf) — we can map fields to our SOC2 artifacts.
3) Confirm budget ballpark and procurement timeline so we can size Dedicated vs Dedicated+Burst.

Proposed next steps / owners:
- Sean (me): run a quick capacity simulation from your sample data and send recommended pool sizes by Tue 9/8.
- Marissa (CC): will join the deep-dive to map SLOs to routing and ops runbook.
- Karthik (CC): will own the topology sketch and quantify batch/cache tradeoffs in the deep-dive.
- OpsWave: confirm availability for a 60-minute technical deep-dive (recommended window: Wed 9/9 or Thu 9/10 morning PT).

Attachments: opswave_metrics_sample.csv (sample traffic), OpsWave_SOC2_Request.pdf (security checklist stub).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with two time options once you confirm availability.

Best,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(sean.gallagher@redwood.ai)

From: Lydia Park <lpark@opswave.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Cho <bcho@opswave.com>, procurement@opswave.com
Date: 2026-09-05T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + technical notes (OpsWave)

Sean — thanks for the clear summary. Confirms everything we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- Burst behavior: yes, promotions typically create short spikes up to ~3x baseline for 5–20 minutes; we need fast warm-up or pre-warm strategies rather than cold starts.
- Budget: for FY27 we have a target range of $150k–$250k for inference stack spend (flexible depending on demonstrated unit economics).
- Security: attaching a short vendor security questionnaire (opswave_security_questions.xlsx) — Marissa, if you can map these to SOC2 artifacts that would be great.

Procurement contact is procurement@opswave.com (copied). Ben will coordinate PO/contract specifics once we have a sizing estimate.

Availability: Wed 9/9 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu 9/10 09:00–10:00 PT work for our engineering + infra.

B) Reserved pool + managed burst nodes + proactive prefix cache strategy (better tail latency guarantees)

If you can include rough cost delta and expected p95 for each option that will help procurement decide.

Marissa
